one_liner: Research Clang 9 fork adding [[clang::jit]]: templates instantiated at run time; beats dynamic-size Eigen, ties size-specialized AoT.
what_it_does: ClangJIT is a fork of LLVM/Clang 9.0 (cxxjit branch) where a function template marked [[clang::jit]] and built with -fjit at compile and link time can receive non-constant values for its non-type template parameters and strings naming types for its type parameters; the call instantiates and compiles that specialization at run time. Source stays ordinary C++ apart from the attribute and the runtime template arguments, so the programmer gets fixed-size or fixed-type code paths without enumerating them ahead of time. It targets two problems the wiki names: long compile times from instantiating many templates, and slow generic code paths when sizes or types are only known at run time.
how_it_is_fast: Runtime specialization: matrix sizes read at run time become template arguments, so Eigen takes its fixed-size path, where the optimizer sees constant trip counts and can fully unroll and vectorize. The compiler embeds a serialized AST of the translation unit, its IR and the original command line in the binary; on the first call the runtime (__clang_jit in clang/lib/CodeGen/JIT.cpp) reads the AST with ASTReader, instantiates the template through Sema, generates code with the stored -O3 options, links the program's IR as available_externally for inlining and loads the result with LLVM ORC. Later calls hit a hash-table cache keyed by the template key, the non-type argument bytes and the type strings.
when_to_use: Research or prototyping of run-time template specialization in C++, for example reproducing the SC19 P3HPC ClangJIT paper (arXiv 1904.08555).
Template-heavy numeric kernels (Eigen-style small fixed-size matrices) where the sizes or scalar types are only known at run time and few of the possible combinations are used in any one run.
Codes where instantiating every size/type combination ahead of time inflates build time: the wiki's build drops from 9.7 s (float/double/long double with dispatch) to 3.5 s.
Long-running jobs that call the JIT function once and loop inside it, so the one-time compile and the per-call dispatch are amortised.
when_not_to_use: Production code: the fork has had no commits since 2019-12-30, is based on LLVM 9.0, and crash and build reports (#17 UD2 trap with Blaze expression templates, #25 segfault on cxxjit-ni-9.0, #28 'Declaration may not be in a Comdat!' with the wiki's type-string example, #30 '-fjit' unknown) remain open.

When the sizes or types are few and known: an AoT build specialized to the size ties the JIT (1.01 vs 1.0 s, 8.45 vs 8.34 s, 35.1 vs 35.3 s), so a switch over fixed-size instantiations gets the same speed with a stock compiler.
Hot call sites that call a JIT template in a tight loop: issue #31 measured about 93 ns per call of an already-compiled empty [[clang::jit]] function.
Larger matrices: the gain over dynamic-size Eigen falls from about 8x at size 3 to 2.4x at size 7 and 1.03x at size 16.
Start-up-sensitive or size-sensitive binaries: the program carries its serialized AST and IR and links the Clang/LLVM libraries to compile at run time; compile latency is not reported.

integration.form: source-drop — build the whole LLVM/Clang fork (wiki CMake recipe with LLVM_ENABLE_PROJECTS=llvm;clang;openmp) and compile and link with its clang++ -fjit
integration.dependencies: the forked Clang/LLVM 9.0 toolchain and its libraries at run time; CUDA runtime (-lcudart) for the device-code JIT path present in the source
integration.min_toolchain: the fork's own clang++ (LLVM 9.0.0 base); the wiki's Clang was built with GCC 8.2.0 in RelWithDebInfo mode
integration.platforms: Linux documented (benchmarked on an Intel Xeon E5-2699); Windows and Visual Studio support asked about in open issues #21 and #22 with no documented answer; source contains a CUDA device JIT path that the wiki does not document
integration.thread_safety: Not documented on the wiki. The runtime guards the instantiation cache with a global mutex and serializes all compilation under a second global mutex (clang/lib/CodeGen/JIT.cpp), so concurrent calls are safe but contend.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — the C++ source changes only by adding [[clang::jit]] and passing runtime template arguments, but it needs the forked compiler; stock compilers reject runtime template arguments.

gotchas: Harness gap: the runtime rows exclude JIT compilation time and the wiki never reports it, so the end-to-end cost (AST deserialization, Sema instantiation and -O3 codegen on the first call) is unknown; the benchmark also calls the JIT function once with the loop inside, which hides the about 93 ns per-call dispatch (global mutex plus hashing of the argument bytes and type strings in __clang_jit) that issue #31 measured.

The win is over Eigen's dynamic-size path, not over AoT code quality: AoT built for the same fixed size matches the JIT within 1-2 percent at every size, and at size 16 the JIT is slightly slower (35.3 vs 35.1 s).

The benchmark never uses m after the timed loop (no output or checksum), is a single run timed with system_clock, and its main(), the Eigen version and the ClangJIT commit are not published, so it cannot be rerun exactly.

Language restrictions: decltype(auto) and other body-dependent deduction are unavailable on JIT templates, explicit specializations are not JIT-compiled, a runtime pointer argument creates one instantiation per pointer value, and type strings are parsed in the declaring context with unspecified visibility of later-declared types.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Most siblings are managed-runtime JITs (HotSpot, .NET, Bun, LuaJIT) beating C or C++ programs; ClangJIT is C++ specialized at run time and only beats generic C++ code. Proteus (llnl/proteus) is the closer alternative: it specializes host, CUDA and HIP code on runtime values through a Clang pass plugin or compiler-independent frontends on LLVM 19-22 without a forked compiler, so pick ClangJIT only to study [[clang::jit]]'s template-level semantics (runtime non-type and type-string template arguments) or the SC19 paper.
verified_claims_summary: Author's wiki benchmark (Eigen loop m = Ones + 0.00005*(m + m*m), double, 40,000,000 repeats, -march=native -ffast-math -O3, Intel Xeon E5-2699, JIT compile time excluded): JIT fixed-size code 1.0, 8.34 and 35.3 s for sizes 3, 7 and 16 vs 8.05, 20 and 36.2 s for dynamic-size AoT Eigen and 1.01, 8.45 and 35.1 s for AoT code specialized to that size. Build time with the JIT is 3.5 s vs 9.7 s for AoT float/double/long double with dispatch and 5.3 s for AoT double only.
status_note: Abandoned research prototype (cxxjit branch last updated 2019-12-30, cxxjit-ni-9.0 2020-01-16, LLVM 9.0 base, open crash and build issues), Apache-2.0 WITH LLVM-exception; worth reading as a reference design, not as a dependency.
